recommendation: Keep the audit commit. No FHIR-14075 source follow-up is needed in core; future changes to operation GET behavior should be handled through later issues such as FHIR-51046 rather than restoring the older primitive-only wording.
issue_request: FHIR-14075 was Published/Persuasive with Modification for FHIR-core operations. It asked to clarify the old operations.html wording that appeared to require both primitive inputs and a single Resource output parameter named return in order to invoke an operation using GET; the approved modification replaced idempotent wording with the affectsState concept and a reference to its definition.
initial_application: The Jira comment records svn revision 14270, corresponding to git commit c208aebcec645ec8dc393a60cd798908ba57f63c. That commit replaced the confusing sentence with a GET eligibility list and a separate return-parameter response paragraph. Later commit 1e03edb85ba9a6148f1aab515bd3bd6713029b34 removed an idempotent/HTTP-spec parenthetical from adjacent Operation Request guidance and linked affectsState directly.
additional_context: source/hierarchy.xml actively includes source/operations.html in the build, and OperationDefinition remains active through source/fhir.ini and source/hierarchy.xml. Later FHIR-51046 changed the older simple/primitive-parameter boundary to the current datatypes-with-corresponding-search-types rule and is already represented on the combined branch. Later response issues, including FHIR-28292 and FHIR-24869, refined the return-parameter paragraph without re-coupling it to GET eligibility. Zulip searches found historical discussion quoting the old confusing sentence and discussing affectsState, but no conflicting current decision.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. No source edit was needed because source/operations.html now states the single-return response behavior separately from the GET criteria, links GET eligibility to affectsState, and has been consistently updated by the later FHIR-51046 search-type clarification.
